AI-driven engineering with Claude Code

Agents do the work. Humans own intent and the merge.

A harness is every control around an agent that a person wrote, can read and can change by pull request: context, permissions, hooks, review gates. This playbook sets the standard, gives you the files, and walks through six production use cases.

IntentA person states the goal
Refined briefGoal, requirements, acceptance
HooksPreToolUse can block (exit 2)
Rulesdeny, ask, allow
Tool runsOn a branch, audited
GatesCI, AI review
MergeA human approves
Human decisionControl written as codeAgent work

Standards

Eleven short chapters: principles, anatomy, context, orchestration, hooks, permissions, MCP, gates, security, cost, maturity.

Templates

CLAUDE.md, settings.json, three tested PowerShell hooks, reviewer subagents, the orchestrate skill, a PR template.

Scenarios

Repo bootstrap, ticket to PR, CI fix loop, dependency upgrade, Terraform review, incident triage.

Chapter 01

Anatomy of a harness

Outer layers decide, inner layers do. Pick a layer to see the file that defines it, who owns it, and who reviews a change to it.

Chapters 04 and 05

Guardrail simulator

Try a tool call against the template settings.json and the guard hooks. The hook runs first; a call goes through only when the hook exits 0 and no deny or ask rule matches. This is a browser copy of the patterns, for learning. The PowerShell hooks and their Pester tests are the real thing.

Chapter 03

The orchestrate workflow

Refine, plan, delegate in parallel, verify, report. Speed comes from parallel work and right-sized models, never from skipping verification.

Pick the model and effort for a subagent

Choose the kind of work. Go up one level only after an attempt failed on reasoning, not on a vague brief.

Chapter 07

Review gates

Every change from an agent passes the same stack. Pick a change and see where it stops. AI review can raise a flag but never replaces the human approval, and agents never merge.

Scenario library

Six production use cases

Each one has the same sections: situation, trigger, who does what, flow, guardrails, gates, failure modes, metrics and a try-it block. They are recommended designs and say what has not been run end to end.
